clue.text: Group of supporters following a new team

parts.note: taken as written
a club is a sports team

explanation.surface: A newly formed side picks up its first band of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is an organised body of admirers of a team or performer.

clue.text: Fantastic cut in price makes you feverish

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: cut means the word for fantastic loses its tail

parts.note: brill, informal British short for brilliant

explanation.surface: A wonderful price reduction leaves a shopper in a fever of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Fantastic cut looks like a great discount. Brill is British slang for brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Febrile means relating to fever, or nervously excited.

clue.text: Kiss amorously then fasten garment

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
to tie is to secure

explanation.surface: A couple embrace and then do up their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is a strip of fabric worn knotted round the collar.

clue.text: Something cowboy might throw, upset in cross altercation

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top
in signals the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of cross and the start of altercation

explanation.surface: A rancher hurls something during an angry quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset looks like the cowboy's mood; in a down clue it turns the run of letters over.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope with a running noose that a cowboy throws to catch cattle.

clue.text: Headwear cricketer put on that opener's lost

indicators.note: in a down clue the cricketer is set on top of what follows

parts.note: a bowler delivers the ball in cricket

indicators.note: the opening letter of that is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer dons a hat after the opening batsman is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: Opener reads as cricket's opening batsman, but it is the first letter of that.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler hat is a hard, round-crowned felt hat, also called a derby.

clue.text: Annoys aristocrats in street? On the contrary

indicators.note: in says one word is placed inside the other
on the contrary reverses the stated roles, so the street goes inside the aristocrats rather than the reverse

parts.note: peers are members of the nobility

explanation.surface: A question about whether nobles wandering the road make a nuisance of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: On the contrary flips the stated container: the street is placed within the nobles, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone is to bother or harass them repeatedly.

clue.text: Navigate vessel around current lake

indicators.note: around means the vessel goes round the other letters

parts.note: a pot is a container
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Steering a boat round a lake against the flow.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessel suggests a ship; it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to steer or guide a craft along a course.

clue.text: Scared, Charlie moves lower and lower — this cannot be criticised

indicators.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet; it shifts one place further down this down entry, rearranging the word

parts.note: taken as written, the word whose Charlie is shifted
something that lows or moos

explanation.surface: A frightened person keeps sinking lower and lower.
explanation.walkthrough: Lower and lower reads as falling further; the first lower moves C one place down, the second is a mooing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea or institution treated as beyond question or criticism.

clue.text: Demanding one fellow supports former lover

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath the ex

parts.note: an ex
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man stands by his former partner who is making demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or requiring much, as in an exacting boss.

clue.text: Remove sign of damage

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a mark or score on a surface

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as getting rid of a blemish, but the word is both the withdrawing and the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratch means to withdraw an entrant from a contest and also a thin scrape mark.

clue.text: Male deer maybe spotted something with sharp teeth

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, though also a male rabbit or hare, hence maybe
saw, past tense of see

explanation.surface: A walker glimpses a stag and then something toothy in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: The sharp-toothed thing sounds like a predator; it is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucksaw is a wood-cutting saw in an H-shaped frame, its blade lined with teeth.

clue.text: Cur liked new doughnuts primarily going more jammy

indicators.note: new tells us to make something fresh out of the remaining letters of cur liked
going means the letter picked out of doughnuts leaves the fodder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means only the leading letter of doughnuts is used

parts.note: its first letter, picked out by primarily

explanation.surface: A mongrel that liked fresh doughnuts gets a sweeter deal than most.
explanation.walkthrough: Jammy is British slang for lucky; the doughnuts and jam make it look like a food clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Jammy is informal British for fortunate, so more jammy is a comparative of good fortune.

clue.text: River not bad temperature for mouse

indicators.note: bad signals the words river not are spoiled into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that a river is not unpleasantly hot for a small rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: Mouse is not the animal but a quiet, retiring person.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy, timid person who keeps to themselves is called a mouse, the same character as a withdrawn introvert.

clue.text: European opening competition

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: The curtain-raising contest of a pan-continental tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a single contest in a sporting programme.

clue.text: Use social networking site in plane, say, on the way back

indicators.note: in places the networking site inside the tree
on the way back means the word for the plane is read in reverse

parts.note: a plane is a type of tree, hence say
X is the current name of the site formerly called Twitter

explanation.surface: Someone posts on social media during a flight home.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane is the tree, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert strength or influence is to bring it to bear, to employ it.

clue.text: Insect eaten by ultra wild adult spider

indicators.note: eaten by means the insect is swallowed inside the other letters
wild means the letters of ultra run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A big spider devours a bug in a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider of warm regions.

clue.text: Hospital operation put an end to game

parts.note: to scotch a rumour or plan is to stop it dead

explanation.surface: A hospital procedure brings a contest to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground pastime of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: Beer supply rising in China

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a crop is a harvest or yield, a supply of produce
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news item about increasing beer stocks in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is fine crockery, not the country; the capital letter disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is the fine ceramic ware traditionally called china.

clue.text: Celebrity's fabulous heavenly body

definitions.note: read as celebrity is, the 's linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: super, informal for excellent
a star in the sky

explanation.surface: A gossip line praising a famous person's wonderful figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavenly body reads as a compliment on someone's looks, but it is a star in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstar is an extremely famous performer or sportsperson.

clue.text: Raise the pitch of stringed instrument held by nurse

indicators.note: held by puts the instrument inside the nurse

parts.note: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
a harp is plucked on its strings

explanation.surface: A nurse holds a harp and tunes it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To sharpen a note is to raise it in pitch, as a musician tightening a string.

clue.text: Ideal total

explanation.walkthrough: Total looks like a sum, but it is the adjective, as in a perfect fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect means flawless and also complete or utter, as in a perfect stranger.

clue.text: Start some homebrew in celebration

indicators.note: some means just part of the run of words is taken

parts.note: the letters span the end of homebrew, all of in and the start of celebration

explanation.surface: A party where a little home-made beer is served.
explanation.walkthrough: Start here is a verb meaning to flinch, not to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump or flinch suddenly, as when someone recoils in pain.

clue.text: Reminder about missing mackintosh initially? More like an anorak

indicators.note: about signals the remaining letters are turned around into a new order
missing means the picked letter is dropped from reminder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of mackintosh is taken

parts.note: its first letter, picked out by initially

explanation.surface: A note that a raincoat has gone missing, then a jab about wearing an anorak.
explanation.walkthrough: An anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, not just a coat; the mackintosh adds to the rainwear decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorak is British slang for a geek, so more like one is more geeky.

clue.text: Hospital department next to HR with a large entrance

parts.note: ENT, ear, nose and throat
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital ward sits beside the personnel office with a big doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Entrance is a verb, to delight, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate or bewitch, the verb sense of entrance.

clue.text: In favour of wearing an item of protective clothing

indicators.note: wearing means one part is clothed by the other, so the two words nest

parts.note: taken as written
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone keen on putting on a piece of safety gear.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is worn over clothes to protect them from dirt or spills.

clue.text: Unfortunately all masters almost suspect something

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
almost means the phrase stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: taken as written, before its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A school's teachers all fall under suspicion of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom for sensing that something is wrong or underhand.

clue.text: H Rider Haggard novel left on female's mantelpiece

parts.note: She is an 1887 adventure novel by H Rider Haggard
F for female

explanation.surface: A Victorian adventure novel left on a woman's fireplace shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantelpiece is the ledge above a fireplace, a kind of shelf.

clue.text: City guides on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: leads, as in shows the way

explanation.surface: Local tour guides heard on a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a major English city in West Yorkshire.

clue.text: Quietly return to judge

parts.note: to resume is to go back to something after a break

explanation.surface: A court official is quietly sent back to the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: Judge is a verb here, not the person on the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to suppose or reckon something true, a sense of judging without proof.

clue.text: Studio swallowed story by director finally

parts.note: ate, past tense of eat
a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of director is used

parts.note: its last letter, picked out by finally

explanation.surface: A film director's tale is believed in a production studio.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop.

clue.text: Record reduced by 50 per cent — a great deal!

indicators.note: reduced means the word for record is cut short at its tail

parts.note: to note something is to record it
fifty per cent is a half

explanation.surface: A record price cut by half is a bargain to shout about.
explanation.walkthrough: Not half is a British exclamation meaning very much indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: The British exclamation not half means greatly or emphatically yes, matching a great deal.

clue.text: Hole in trunk perhaps is torn carelessly by student

indicators.note: carelessly means the letters of is torn are thrown together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L for learner

explanation.surface: A student rips a hole in a travel trunk through clumsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The trunk is an elephant's, not luggage; perhaps flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's trunk is its elongated nose, ending in two openings for breathing.
